runtime_checks: Freeze the actual Codex binary, reviewed config.toml or its absence, effective MCP-name inventory and all project configuration inputs before model execution.
Disable every actual MCP server before startup and verify effective MCP, plugin, hook and Skill controls without persisting credential-bearing config.
Use a single ephemeral thread and active turn; compare effective provider/model/effort/cwd and stop on rerouting.
Route only the six namespaced dynamic operations to the original bounded Engine; reject native approvals, permission requests, user-input requests and unexpected effect events.
Keep startup controls and empty environments on every thread/turn. Configuration layers must not re-enable delegation or redirect the approved provider.
Require actual usage, correlated terminal state, and owned Codex/MCP process and pipe cleanup before success.

observed_controls.code_mode_exec: handler disabled; its visible declaration is not an OS execution capability
observed_controls.direct_apply_patch: rejected before file access because no execution environment is available
observed_controls.collaboration_spawn: unsupported after agents.enabled=false; zero child model requests and child thread starts
observed_controls.dynamic_operation: craft_host/build_files_list roundtrip observed at item/tool/call Gate
observed_controls.cleanup: Windows owned Job empty, root exited, stdout/stderr closed

qualification_limits: Extra inactive or resource-only helper declarations may remain visible; raw tool count is not the effect-permission contract.
No real provider/model, original business target, or business build acceptance is implied by local canned Responses verification.
Single-response and aggregate token/cost hard caps are unsupported; only explicitly accepted wall/refine limits and actual usage audit are supported.
Frozen engineering commands are not an operating-system sandbox against malicious application code.
